key_results: ΔB correlates with output-level bias (|r|=0.84, p<0.001); detects biased checkpoints with ROC AUC 0.65-0.99; 3-50× less compute than output benchmarks

title: Configurational diversity of metabotropic glutamate receptor complexes with beta-arrestins
task: Map mGluR/β-arrestin interaction diversity, stoichiometry, and megacomplex formation
key_results: mGluRs couple to β-arrs with 2:1 or 2:2 stoichiometry; mGluRs form megacomplexes simultaneously binding β-arr1/β-arr2 or β-arr/G proteins
comments: SiMPull assay elegantly quantifies both interaction strength and stoichiometry at single-molecule resolution, revealing previously unappreciated complexity in GPCR transducer coupling.

hypotheses.hypothesis: mGluRs exhibit variable β-arr coupling strength and distinct stoichiometries compared to family A GPCRs
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; 2:1 and 2:2 stoichiometries observed with variable apparent strength

hypotheses.hypothesis: β-arr interactions involve both C-terminal 'tail' and intracellular loop 'core' binding sites
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; combinatorial mutagenesis maps contributions of tail and core interactions

hypotheses.hypothesis: mGluRs can simultaneously bind multiple transducers forming megacomplexes
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; cells form megacomplexes with β-arr1/β-arr2 or β-arr/G proteins

title: Structural basis of active state coupling of metabotropic glutamate receptor 8 to beta-arrestins
task: Determine structural basis of mGluR8 coupling to β-arrestins and desensitization mechanism
key_results: Cryo-EM reveals distinct mGluR8/β-arr1 complex orientation with transducer-specific active states; steric desensitization mechanism involves both β-arr subunits and lipid bilayer interactions
comments: Integrative approach combining EM, cryo-EM, FRET, and MD simulations provides comprehensive mechanistic insight, though the physiological relevance of the observed 'active-like' conformation warrants further validation.

hypotheses.hypothesis: mGluR8 adopts distinct active conformations depending on transducer (G protein vs β-arr)
hypotheses.result: Confirmed by cryo-EM structures showing transducer-specific differences

hypotheses.hypothesis: β-arrestin desensitizes mGluR8 through steric mechanisms involving both arrestin subunits
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; complex shows unique orientation compared to family A GPCR/β-arr structures

title: Oxidative stress-responsive cell wall remodeling depends on phosphate in Candida albicans

key_results: Phosphate-depleted cells fail to recruit mobile outer polysaccharides into rigid wall core during H₂O₂ exposure; wildtype cells reinforce wall scaffold through selective polymer redistribution
comments: Solid-state NMR provides valuable atomic-level mechanistic detail, but the study would benefit from quantitative measures of wall mechanical strength changes under different conditions.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Oxidative stress in phosphate-replete cells triggers selective polymer redistribution to strengthen wall

title: MutexaGPT: an intuition-to-design translator for physics-based enzyme engineering
task: Translate enzyme engineering intuition into physics-based design through multi-agent LLM interface
key_results: Successfully engineered halide methyltransferase for bulkier substrates and bidomain amylase for enhanced activity at lower temperature; LLM generates actionable mutation libraries from plain-English design concepts
comments: Novel integration of LLM agents with high-throughput molecular modeling democratizes physics-guided design, though validation of predicted variants against experimental data would strengthen the framework.

hypotheses.result: Confirmed; engineered variants show enhanced substrate accommodation and/or lower-temperature activity

title: Deficiency of protein kinase Cδ reprograms macrophage immunometabolism to suppress pyroptosis and stabilize atherosclerotic plaques
task: Determine whether PKCδ deficiency reprograms macrophage immunometabolism to suppress pyroptosis and stabilize atherosclerotic plaques
key_results: PKCδ expression elevated in ruptured plaques; PKCδ deletion reduced necrotic core and increased fibrous cap thickness; PKCδ deficiency enhanced oxidative phosphorylation and elevated α-ketoglutarate, reducing NLRP3 inflammasome activation and pyroptosis; dimethyl α-ketoglutarate supplementation provided similar protection
comments: The mechanistic link between PKCδ-regulated mitochondrial metabolism (via α-KG/PIK3AP1/mTORC2) and pyroptosis suppression is well-integrated, offering both understanding of plaque stability and a potential metabolite-based therapeutic intervention.

model_io.model: LDL receptor knockout mice with global and myeloid-specific PKCδ deletion

hypotheses.hypothesis: PKCδ deletion stabilizes atherosclerotic plaques by suppressing macrophage pyroptosis
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; reduced necrotic core and increased fibrous cap in both global and myeloid-specific models

hypotheses.hypothesis: PKCδ deficiency shifts macrophage metabolism toward oxidative phosphorylation and elevates α-KG, reducing NLRP3 inflammasome activation
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; metabolic reprogramming and PIK3AP1/mTORC2 activation suppress pyroptosis

hypotheses.hypothesis: α-ketoglutarate supplementation mimics PKCδ deficiency in stabilizing plaques
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; dimethyl α-ketoglutarate provided similar protective effects

title: Competitive binding between WSB2 and XIAP regulates O-GlcNAcase MGEA5 ubiquitination to control prospermatogonia fate
task: Determine mechanism of WSB2-mediated regulation of O-GlcNAcase MGEA5 in prospermatogonia development
key_results: Wsb2 knockout mice exhibited rapid ProSG depletion and SCOS-like phenotypes; WSB2 stabilizes MGEA5 by competitive binding to prevent XIAP-mediated ubiquitination; loss of WSB2 elevates O-GlcNAcylation, causes DNA double-strand breaks; O-GlcNAc transferase inhibitor OSMI-1 restored ProSG population
comments: The non-canonical WSB2 function independent of ECS complex assembly is noteworthy, and the mechanistic link to O-GlcNAcylation-induced DSBs provides a rational therapeutic target, though in vivo OSMI-1 efficacy requires clinical validation.

model_io.model: Wsb2 knockout mouse model and in vitro cell systems

hypotheses.hypothesis: WSB2 stabilizes MGEA5 through competitive binding and prevents XIAP-mediated ubiquitination
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; decreased MGEA5 expression in Wsb2 KO leads to elevated O-GlcNAcylation and DSB

hypotheses.hypothesis: O-GlcNAc transferase inhibition restores ProSG in Wsb2 KO mice
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; OSMI-1 treatment effectively restored ProSG population

title: Human testis-specific TTRP regulates circadian clock as an evolutionarily young natural antisense transcript of PER2
task: Characterize TTRP, a testis-specific PER2 antisense transcript, as a novel circadian clock regulator
key_results: TTRP emerged ~8.6 Mya in higher Hominoidea; overlaps PER2 and interferes with its transcription; interacts with PER2/BMAL1/CRY2 and promotes PER2/CRY1 turnover; alters circadian period/amplitude; prolongs brood-interval and increases sperm motility in mice
comments: The discovery of a recently evolved human-specific circadian regulator is intriguing and suggests ongoing evolution of clock circuits, though functional consequences beyond male fertility remain to be explored.

model_io.model: Human cells and mouse testis with TTRP expression modulation

hypotheses.hypothesis: TTRP regulates circadian clock through PER2 and CRY protein turnover
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; TTRP interacts with clock proteins and promotes PER2/CRY1 degradation

hypotheses.hypothesis: TTRP influences male reproductive phenotypes through circadian regulation
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; TTRP knock-in prolongs brood-interval and increases high-motility sperm ratio

title: Placental TRPV2 supports trophoblast function and normal fetal development
task: Elucidate TRPV2's role in placental development and fetal outcome
key_results: Trpv2 deletion causes fetal growth restriction and embryonic lethality; TRPV2 is required for SynTII differentiation in trophoblast
comments: The study convincingly localized TRPV2 function to trophoblast via cell-type-specific knockouts, though the molecular mechanism of ion channel function in syncytial differentiation remains to be determined.

model_io.model: Mouse Trpv2 knockout and trophoblast stem cell CRISPR

hypotheses.hypothesis: TRPV2 is non-redundantly required in trophoblast for normal placental development
hypotheses.result: Confirmed via trophoblast-specific Trpv2 knockout showing growth restriction phenotype

title: Bioactive ultrasound preserves periosteal vascular architecture during mechanical unloading
task: Investigate whether low-intensity pulsed ultrasound (LIPUS) preserves periosteal vascular architecture during mechanical unloading
key_results: Mechanical unloading disrupted periosteal vasculature and increased hypoxia; LIPUS attenuated bone loss, suppressed osteoclast activation, and preserved periosteal vascular architecture; vascular preservation positively correlated with bone mass and inversely with cortical hypoxia
comments: The identification of periosteal vascular preservation as a key component of skeletal adaptation is important, and LIPUS's multi-target effects on osteoclasts, osteoblasts, and vasculature suggest therapeutic potential, though long-term efficacy in spaceflight remains to be tested.

model_io.model: Murine hindlimb unloading model with daily LIPUS treatment

hypotheses.hypothesis: LIPUS preserves periosteal vascular architecture during mechanical unloading and maintains bone homeostasis
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; LIPUS suppressed osteoclast activation and partially preserved osteoblasts while maintaining vasculature

hypotheses.hypothesis: Periosteal vascular architecture preservation is associated with attenuated bone loss and reduced hypoxia
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; positive correlation between vascular preservation and bone mass, inverse correlation with cortical hypoxia

title: ATP-independent unfolding of ubiquitin by Ufd1 initiates Cdc48/p97-mediated substrate processing
task: Elucidate ATP-independent ubiquitin unfolding mechanism by Ufd1 UT3 domain in Cdc48/p97-mediated substrate processing
key_results: Ufd1 UT3 domain specifically binds two K48-linked ubiquitins and unfolds one by inserting C-terminal β-strand into hydrophobic cleft; simultaneous dual binding required to overcome unfolding energy barrier; UT3-unfolded ubiquitin captured by Npl4 and Cdc48/p97; unfolding-defective Ufd1 mutants compromise Cdc48/p97 function in vitro and in cells
comments: The structural mechanism revealing how protein-protein interactions unfold the remarkably stable ubiquitin is elegant and well-supported by biochemical and cellular evidence, providing molecular insight into AAA-ATPase-mediated protein extraction.

model_io.model: Biochemical in vitro assays with recombinant Ufd1, Npl4, Cdc48/p97, and ubiquitin
Cell-based assays with unfolding-defective Ufd1 mutants

hypotheses.hypothesis: Ufd1 UT3 domain unfolds ubiquitin in an ATP-independent manner through dual K48-ubiquitin binding
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; simultaneous UT3 binding to two ubiquitins required to overcome unfolding energy barrier

hypotheses.hypothesis: Unfolding-defective Ufd1 mutants compromise Cdc48/p97-mediated substrate processing
hypotheses.result: Confirmed in vitro and in cells

title: Nceh1 protects against myocardial ischemia/reperfusion injury by suppressing oxidative stress and apoptosis
task: Determine whether Nceh1 protects against myocardial ischemia/reperfusion injury via oxidative stress suppression
key_results: Nceh1 overexpression markedly attenuated MI/R injury; DNA methylation of cg14338526 inversely associated with Nceh1 mRNA and CAD mortality; Nceh1 activates Nrf2/HO-1 pathway to suppress oxidative stress and apoptosis
comments: The mechanistic pathway (Nceh1 → Nrf2/HO-1 → reduced ROS/apoptosis) is well-supported, though the functional link between epigenetic methylation and cardioprotection would benefit from in vivo validation.

model_io.model: Rat MI/R model and H9C2 cardiomyocyte injury model
Human CAD cohort (n=933) with DNA methylation profiling

hypotheses.hypothesis: Nceh1 suppresses MI/R injury through Nrf2/HO-1 pathway activation
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; ML-385 pretreatment abolished protective effects

hypotheses.hypothesis: DNA methylation of cg14338526 inversely predicts Nceh1 expression and CAD mortality
hypotheses.result: Confirmed via correlation analysis in 933 CAD patients

title: Two postnatal mouse models with Pth1r deletion reproduce limb phenotype for Blomstrand chondrodysplasia

key_results: Two inducible Pth1r deletion models (Acan-CreERT2 and Gli1-CreERT2) exhibited dwarfism with shortened long bones and epiphyseal dysplasia; increased hypertrophic chondrocytes and loss of growth-plate architecture; Gli1 model showed complete growth-plate loss at juvenile and adult timepoints
comments: These complementary inducible models provide important tools for dissecting postnatal PTH1R signaling, though the comparative advantages of Acan vs. Gli1 drivers and tissue-type specific roles require further functional investigation.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Chondrocyte-specific or osteoprogenitor-specific Pth1r deletion reproduces BOCD-like skeletal phenotypes

title: Overexpression of miR-144-3p inhibits the expression of NLRP3 in fibroblast-like synoviocytes of osteoarthritis

key_results: miR-144-3p overexpression significantly reduced NLRP3, ASC, pro-caspase-1 mRNA/protein and IL-1β/TNF-α release in LPS-stimulated FLS; in vivo MIA model showed reduced synovial inflammation and cartilage damage

Rat osteoarthritis-like joint injury model (MIA intra-articular injection)

hypotheses.hypothesis: miR-144-3p overexpression inhibits LPS-induced FLS proliferation and NLRP3 inflammasome activation

hypotheses.hypothesis: miR-144-3p intervention alleviates OA-like pathology in vivo

title: ALKBH5 acts as a regulator  of hair follicle telogen-to-anagen transition in mice
task: Elucidate ALKBH5's role in regulating hair follicle stem cell activation during telogen-anagen transition via m6A methylation
key_results: Alkbh5 deletion promotes HFSC activation/proliferation and accelerates telogen-anagen transition; ALKBH5 loss increases m6A methylation of Mcam mRNA, stabilizing it via YTHDF1 binding; Mcam knockdown impairs HFSC proliferation through reduced Wnt responsiveness; balanced ALKBH5/METTL3 m6A regulation required
comments: The study elegantly demonstrates m6A-mediated post-transcriptional regulation of hair cycle progression, identifying a balanced methylation mechanism, though the upstream signals triggering ALKBH5 downregulation during late telogen remain unclear.
